posts.content:
As Airtable's CCO, I spend a lot of time with customers deploying agents. The ones who are succeeding all took the same, unglamorous step first. They built the system before they deployed the agent.

I know, that's not the advice anyone wants to hear right now. New models ship every few days, each measurably smarter than the last. And the pull to just point Opus 5 at your business and say “go” is almost irresistible. 

But a recent VentureBeat survey found that 57% of enterprises have traced a wrong agent answer back to missing or inconsistent business context. Just because the intelligence is there, doesn’t mean the context follows.

Most agents default to reading whatever they can find — email, docs, Slack, transcripts — and end up reconstructing your business from a dozen unreconciled descriptions. When they work inside a structured, relational system your team already operates in, the difference is more than just accuracy — it’s immediacy. The answer is tailored to your business, and the work is already in motion before anyone sits down in the morning.

That's the shift we're building toward at Airtable, and like always, our strategy starts with what our customers are already doing. Here's the full picture, including how four teams are putting agents to work today: https://lnkd.in/gEys293Y

#Airtable selected me as one of the first testers of their new AI app builder called Canvas.

Took me literally 4 minutes to turn an Airtable database I had into a beautiful app I can share with my customers right away (see the video below).

Some of you will think: "But, Vykintas, I've seen way more impressive apps developed with Claude Code or other AI vibe-coding platforms..." And you'll be correct.

You can build nearly anything with the power tools like #Claude Code, however, will it be easy? I always teach my students that "Vibe-coding is accessible. Not easy". Anyone can now develop applications without special education but - if you want to go beyond prototypes and release business grade apps - it will still take a significant amount of effort and time.

Therefore, I often still prefer using no-code tools like Airtable with their built-in AI capabilities over the new more flexible AI tools. While established players like #Airtable take care of the security & scalability... I can just focus on building my apps.

I'm excited to share the next set of features we've shipped in Airtable core product.

Over the past several weeks we have launched:
‣ Timeline nesting: nest records inside other records in Timeline view, up to 7 levels deep
‣ Reschedule dependent records: when a date moves, only the work after it shifts. What you've already finished stays where it is
‣ Default dependency type & buffer: set them once for a table instead of configuring every link by hand
‣ Date dependencies in record templates: templates now carry their dependency types and buffers, so a new project starts fully wired
‣ Date dependency API: read and WRITE dependency type and buffer through the public API

All of it is aimed at making Airtable a stronger home for strategic portfolio management. If you manage projects with dependencies, I think this set will save you real time.

Read more about these features here 👉 https://lnkd.in/gNhnyTWe

Big shout out to the Airtable community for the feedback - it directly helped shape this set of features 😃


OK....back to my agents 😉

posts.content:
Last month, the Airtable Academy team transformed our entire operating system with a fleet of new agents and agentic workflows. This one helped us increase our publishing output by 125% while maintaining learner CSAT and improving our influenced product usage. Check it out👇

For those unfamiliar, Airtable Academy is the home for our customer education programs -- the self-paced courses, certifications, and learning experiences that help Airtable users of all kind (builders, enterprise admins, end-users) be more successful and effective in their work.

And as anyone in customer education knows, good, effective educational content is cross-functional and time-intensive. A single lesson could mean a script in Docs, graphics and visuals in Slides, a walkthrough-ready demo base with dummy data in Airtable, eLearning assets, knowledge checks, additional resources, etc. etc. etc. -- and that's *before* you pull in product SMEs for review, tap extra resources for video editing, or think about where the lesson fits in the wider catalog.

So the team built an agent that collapses all of it into a single Slack thread. Drop your topic in and get back the full bundle: script, deck, demo base, and a complete eLearning module with a quiz. 

With the skills we've built in, it draws on our learner feedback surveys, anchors to our existing catalog and our product roadmap (both stored in Airtable, obv), applies AEO best practices for LLM discoverability, and uses psychometric principles to build the quiz. 

And because our full tech stack has opened their MCPs, it drafts AND it publishes directly into our tools once the human-in-the-loop approves. Our process has become fully headless.

This past quarter, this agent allowed us to publish 125% more content than a normal sprint. Same team. Same time. Learner CSAT held at 8.9 on the new content, and product usage among course completers jumped +130% in the 30 days after.

This won the individual "Builder Prize" and helped us take home the "Team Breakthrough" prize during Airloop, Airtable's internal agent building competition. And now, it runs every day.
